title: Comparing data sets
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:56Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank points cover single-display stem and dot plots and comparing summary measures with box plots, but neither teaches comparing two data sets using back-to-back stem-and-leaf or parallel dot plots, so the new point needs its own card.

draft.title: Comparing data sets
card: A back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot shares one set of stems down the middle. One data set has leaves on the left and the other has leaves on the right.
A parallel dot plot stacks two dot plots on the same number line, one above the other. Both sets can be read against the same scale.
Compare centre first: find the median or mean of each set. Then compare spread: range = highest value − lowest value.

Then compare shape, such as where the data bunches or whether it tails off to one side. Look for outliers, which are values far from the rest. Example: set A is 4, 6, 7, 9, 14 and set B is 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. Both medians are 7, but the range is 10 for A and 4 for B. A is more spread out.
draft.remember: Compare two sets on the same scale: centre, spread, shape and outliers.

a.q: Set P is 3, 5, 6, 8, 13. Set Q is 4, 6, 7, 9, 10. Which set has the larger range?
a.why: The range of P is 13 − 3 = 10. The range of Q is 10 − 4 = 6. Q's highest value is 10, but its range is found by subtracting, so 10 alone is not its range.
a.clue: Subtract the lowest value from the highest for each set.

b.q: Back-to-back plots show quiz scores for two Year 9 classes in Perth. Class 9A has a median of 14 and a range of 6. Class 9B has a median of 14 and a range of 15. Which comparison is correct?
opts: The centres match, but 9B is more spread out
9B has the higher centre and is more spread out
The centres match, and the spreads are the same
9A has the higher centre and is more spread out
b.why: Both medians are 14, so the centres are the same. The range of 9B is 15 and the range of 9A is 6, so 9B is more spread out. A matching centre does not mean matching spread.
b.clue: Compare the medians first, then compare the ranges.

b.best: The centres match, but 9B is more spread out
